claims.evidence: The witness report identifies the item as a car engine but cannot confirm the brand, model, or country of origin.

risks.risk: Internal mechanical failure or seized components.
risks.proof: A video showing the engine being hand-cranked or a compression test report.
risks.if_unproven: as a non-working core for parts only

risks.risk: Incompatibility with the intended vehicle due to unknown engine code.
risks.proof: A clear photo of the engine code stamped on the block (e.g., G4FA, G4KD).
risks.if_unproven: as a generic, low-value scrap engine

risks.risk: Missing or damaged critical sensors and wiring harness.
risks.proof: Close-up photos of all electrical connectors and the complete wiring loom.
risks.if_unproven: as a bare long block without accessories

proof_requests: Photo of the engine model code stamped on the metal engine block.
Video of the crankshaft being turned to prove it is not seized.
Clear photos of the intake and exhaust ports to check for oil sludge or carbon buildup.
Confirmation of the specific vehicle make and year this was pulled from.
response.reason: The specific engine model and brand are unidentified, which is necessary to determine compatibility and market value in Lagos. Without the engine code, it cannot be priced even at a worst-case scenario.
